key_insight: A zero-shot, agentic LLM workflow can extract lung resection pathology fields from clinical narratives with high recall, approaching a supervised baseline without task-specific training.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual abstraction for cancer staging and tumor registry data entry by automating extraction from narrative pathology reports.
method: Developed a zero-shot agentic workflow for 13 CAP synoptic fields.
Benchmarked five open-source generative LLMs against a supervised GatorTron NER-RE baseline.
Used a novel registry-aligned evaluation framework on lung resection pathology reports.
evidence_signal: On the abstract’s evaluation, the supervised baseline reached Micro-F1 0.960, while the best zero-shot model (GPT-OSS-20B) reached Micro-F1 0.893 with recall 0.949.
watch_item: Performance is still below the supervised benchmark, so real-world deployment would need careful validation for field-level accuracy and missed or distorted relations.
paper_title: Prompt, Plan, Extract: Zero-Shot Agentic LLMs Workflows for Lung Pathology Extraction from Clinical Narratives
